newsitem.title: FRANCE: French bank boss freed on day six of siege.
newsitem.headline: French bank boss freed on day six of siege.

text.p: Employees occupying the headquarters of the troubled bank Credit Foncier de France released Chairman Jerome Meyssonnier Wednesday after holding him for six days in a protest against plans to break up the bank.

Meyssonnier, who had been prevented from leaving his office since staff started the occupation Friday, told employees in the building he was "delighted" by their decision to release him, which he said demonstrated their sense of responsbility.

Meyssonnier's declaration followed word from the unions leading the protest that Mayssonnier and several board members who had been held along with him were no longer being barred from leaving the downtown Paris building.
"We are delighted by this opening, which shows the sense of responsibility of everyone and the desire to preserve the image of our company," Meyssonnier said.
The release would help to restart the dialogue on the future of the bank with the help of the government-appointed mediator, Philippe Rouvillois, he added.
Union spokesman Jean-Claude Mabourde said the unions would press their campaign to keep the bank, which was founded 145 years ago by Emperor Napoleon III, intact and in business.
The bank provides cheap home loans to poorer families.
The government wants to break up the group, spin off part of it to another cooperatively run lender and close the rest over time.
